title: Structural Induction Principles for Functional Programmers
review_status: full-text audit complete; algorithm and teaching rationale, no controlled learning-outcome evaluation
sections_checked: structural induction derivation from recursive type constructors
generated Haskell output for standard and parameter-swapping types
lazy bottom caveat and Appendix A algorithm
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2013-12-10; author-hosted TFPIE 2013 paper PDF audited.
evidence_note: Haskell algorithm mechanically produces induction principles from algebraic datatype declarations, including recursive parameter changes. Paper is a method/teaching account, not controlled educational evidence; tool had not yet been introduced to the course, and mutually recursive types are omitted. Lazy bottom requires an extra case.

title: Inferring Parametric Energy Consumption Functions at Different Software Levels: ISA vs. LLVM IR
review_status: full-text audit complete; hardware-measured static analysis trade-off, bounded to XC/XCore evaluation
sections_checked: ISA-to-LLVM energy mapping and model assumptions
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2015-11-04; full author/institution PDF audited.
evidence_note: LLVM IR preserves type/shape information lost at ISA. First benchmark group reports mean errors 3.9% ISA vs 9% LLVM IR; for structured-data group, ISA fails to infer useful functions on some programs while LLVM IR analyzes all with ~3% mean error and 5-6 sec analysis time. Uses XC/XCore and approximate mapping; average instruction energies may under-estimate worst-case energy, so upper-bound soundness is not established by averages.

title: Multiparty Session Types for Safe Runtime Adaptation in an Actor Language (Extended version)
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal protocol-safety result and adaptive DNS feasibility case, no production performance evaluation in this study
sections_checked: EnsembleS actors and generated session-typed skeletons
explicit runtime connection and actor discovery/replacement
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2021-05-14; ECOOP 2021 full proceedings/extended paper PDF audited, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.ECOOP.2021.12.
evidence_note: Multiparty session types preserve protocol order/roles during dynamic actor discovery/replacement; an adaptive DNS scenario demonstrates feasibility and the core calculus proves formal safety/progress. No production reliability/throughput study or adaptation-overhead result in this paper; runtime performance is deferred to cited prior Ensemble work. Protocol compliance does not establish discovered service honesty or semantic correctness.

title: Tidying Up the Address Space
review_status: full-text audit complete; controlled HADES prototype results with explicit ownership/pointer applicability constraints
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2025-10-22; primary arXiv HTML/PDF audited.
evidence_note: On one 16-core Xeon/CrestDB setup across ten pointer data structures and YCSB A/B/C, reports up to 70% lower memory use, 2.5% average throughput reduction and 5% latency increase from tracking, with backend integration reducing a 12GB footprint toward 4GB in YCSB-C. Applicability requires unique ownership, no cached-pointer stability or pointer arithmetic assumptions, explicit annotations, and supported pointer interception; not a general production workload result.
